title: Chlorofluoromethanes, chlorine, and Antarctic ozone

body: In 1974 Molina and Rowland proposed a stratospheric sink for chlorofluoromethanes: chlorine atoms released from those gases catalyze the destruction of ozone. The paper is a chemical mechanism, published before the Antarctic observations. In 1985 Farman, Gardiner, and Shanklin reported "Large losses of total ozone in Antarctica reveal seasonal ClOx/NOx interaction," in Nature, pages 207–210. The title ties the observed spring losses to chlorine and nitrogen oxide chemistry. The Montreal Protocol is the later treaty aimed at substances that deplete the ozone layer; the Ozone Secretariat publishes its text. The 1995 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognized the atmospheric chemistry. A mechanism paper, an observational paper, a treaty, and a prize are four different kinds of claim. The chemistry and the Antarctic losses are the scientific ones.
